prompt:
Image 1 is a grey clay maquette of this figure: follow its pose, its parts and its framing, the whole figure from head to foot filling the square as it does, seen three-quarter front from a little above. It is a crude blockout: take its pose, its parts and its framing, not its stubby proportions. Paint over it completely: no grey clay and no plain smooth shapes may remain. Image 2 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, candle lighting, rim light, muted colours and dark background. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing. The subject, its face, its headgear and every ornament must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns, the fur or the trim from Image 2.

A full-length painted portrait of the Living Monolith, a god that is a single great standing stone: immobile, ancient and aware, in a regal pose: upright and perfectly still. Three-quarter front view, the body and the face turned slightly toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the whole figure fills the height of the square: the top of the slab about 6% from the top edge and the base about 94% from the top, centred, with dark empty space around the silhouette. One figure only: no people, no worshippers, no other creatures, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the top and the edges of the slab that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. As in the style reference, much of the figure falls into deep warm shadow: the candle picks out the upper left of the head, the shoulders and the chest, and the lower body and the far side sink into the dark; it is not evenly lit. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects, no landscape, no horizon and no floor: the dark background runs unbroken to the bottom edge, with only a faint soft shadow under the base.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, loose visible brushwork and soft edges as in the style reference, moderate detail, never a crisp, clean digital illustration; a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the tall slab and its rooted base against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the stone is the pigment in its carved glyphs: dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Nothing in the image glows: the glyphs are pigment in carved grooves. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.

Subject: Body: one tall, rough-hewn slab of grey granite (#7D7A75), about three times as tall as it is wide and a third as thick, its edges weathered and chipped, seen three-quarter front so that its broad face and one narrow side show; no capstone: its top is a plain, flat, broken edge; no moss, no vines, no overgrowth; no face, no eyes, no carved features. Glyphs: rows of deeply carved runic glyphs running down its broad face, the grooves filled with a pigment of dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Base: its foot is rooted in the ground: it rises from a low mound of dark earth and stones, with thick old roots gripping its base.
Paint it as described, the whole figure clearly in view.
